messages:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered for service=auth-service — high 5xx rate detected (5m avg 18%). PD incident: INC123456.

pagerduty: A page was created and routed to on-call. escalation_policy: auth-team.

sara.dev: acking on behalf of leo — jumping in now. digging into edge logs.

leo.oncall: thanks. I'm on call but still finishing a handoff, sara you have it. any region skew?

maya.ops: eu-west1 showing the highest error spike (502/504) ~ 18:42 UTC, us-west1 small bump.

ops-lead: customer-facing routes flagged: /v1/auth/token and /v1/sessions — some rate-limited clients getting 502s. estimating impact to ~0.7% of traffic.

infra-bot: autoscaler triggered +2 replicas on auth-deployment (k8s) at 18:44:11 UTC.

sara.dev: quick dump from the edge:```[edge-proxy] upstream returned 502, conn-reset by peer, TLS handshake OK, keepalive timeout 0.23s, backend=auth-service-3```

leo.oncall: looks like warmup traffic from a canary load generator hit the auth pool while a rolling restart was in progress. coordinator reported prefetch jobs + concurrency spike.

maya.ops: verifying — there was a 10:42 UTC job that reloaded secrets on nodes in eu-west1, combined with cache cold-start. KV cache misses spiked 12x.

ops-lead: immediate mitigations: 1) pause canary traffic 2) add temporary weight to standby pool 3) scale auth pods to +4 and bump connection timeout to 5s. Sara/Leo please confirm actions.

sara.dev: paused canary (loadgen) and shifted weight to standby at 18:46. scaling to +4 in progress. bumping timeout in nginx upstream now.

leo.oncall: scaling finished, nginx timeout patched, starting to see 5xx rate drop — current 5m avg 3.2%.

pagerduty: PagerDuty update: incident INC123456 acknowledged by sara.dev. escalation paused.

ops-lead: hold for 10m observation. we should run a healthcheck sweep against affected routes and collect a sample of failed request IDs for postmortem.

infra-bot: sample failed request ids: [req-84f2, req-84f7, req-84fd] (collected).

maya.ops: customer impact note: internal metrics indicate retries recovered most user requests; small number of failed auths surfaced to integrations (3rd-party). need to notify SRE/customer-success if rollback required.

leo.oncall: putting a temporary rollback window on the recent deploy that overlapped the restart; if errors reappear, we will rollback. current plan: observe until 19:00 UTC then close if stable.

ops-lead: post-incident checklist: capture timeline, include canary schedule, review restart ordering, add KV warmup step, adjust autoscale thresholds. assigning postmortem to sara.dev.

sara.dev: will write postmortem and include mitigation playbook. thanks all. :thumbsup:
